The Node.js Backend internship in short

In the SkillMe Node.js Backend internship you build one of 3 projects, such as CloudVault: RESTful Secure API & Resource Management Hub, a project where you build a REST API with Node.js and Express that stores your notes and links, and keeps each user's items private with a login. In week 1 you set up a Node.js project with Express and build your first API endpoints that return vault items (notes and links) from an in-memory array. By week 4 you add user accounts so each person can register, log in and see only their own vault items. Each milestone is posted on LinkedIn and checked against that week's checklist before it counts. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month.

One of 3 real projects, built over four weeks

Week by week

What each week of the Node.js Backend internship covers

Shown for CloudVault: RESTful Secure API & Resource Management Hub. The other projects follow the same four-week shape.

  1. Week 1 of 4

    Your First Express API

    Beginner2-3 hours

    Set up a Node.js project with Express and build your first API endpoints that return vault items (notes and links) from an in-memory array. You will learn how a server receives a request and sends back JSON.

    What you learn

    • Setting up a Node project with npm init and installing packages
    • Creating an Express server and defining routes
    • Sending JSON responses and using route parameters like /items/:id
    • Testing an API with a browser and Thunder Client or Postman

    What you submit

    • A Node + Express project that starts with node server.js or npm start
    • Three working GET routes: list, single item, and filter by type
    • A .gitignore that excludes node_modules
    • A short demo video calling the routes in Thunder Client or Postman
    How week 1 is reviewed
    • GET /api/items returns all sample items as JSON
    • GET /api/items/1 returns one item and GET /api/items/999 returns status 404 with an error message
    • GET /api/items?type=link returns only links
    • node_modules is not committed to Git
    • The server logs a message showing which port it is running on

    Stretch goal: Add a GET /api/stats route that returns how many notes and how many links exist.

  2. Week 2 of 4

    Full CRUD, Validation & Middleware

    Beginner+2-3 hours

    Turn your read-only API into a full CRUD API so items can be created, updated and deleted, with input validation and correct status codes. You will also write your first custom middleware.

    What you learn

    • The four CRUD operations mapped to POST, GET, PUT/PATCH and DELETE
    • Reading JSON request bodies with express.json()
    • Validating input and returning the right HTTP status codes (200, 201, 400, 404)
    • What middleware is and how to write a simple logger

    What you submit

    • Working create, read, update and delete routes for items
    • Validation with clear 400 error messages
    • A custom logger middleware
    • An exported Thunder Client or Postman collection in the repo
    How week 2 is reviewed
    • Creating an item returns status 201 and the new item
    • Posting an item without a title returns status 400 and a helpful error
    • Updating or deleting an unknown id returns status 404
    • Every request is printed in the terminal by your logger
    • Item routes live in their own router file

    Stretch goal: Add a tags array to items and support GET /api/items?tag=study.

  3. Week 3 of 4

    Saving Data with SQLite & Error Handling

    Intermediate2-3 hours

    Replace the in-memory array with a SQLite database so your data survives a server restart. You will also add search, simple pagination and a central error handler so the API behaves well when things go wrong.

    What you learn

    • Storing data in a SQLite database with basic SQL (CREATE, INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE)
    • Using parameterised queries to avoid SQL injection
    • Pagination and search with query parameters
    • Central error-handling middleware in Express

    What you submit

    • A SQLite-backed API where data survives restarts
    • Search and pagination on the list route
    • A central error-handling middleware
    • A demo video creating an item, restarting the server and fetching it again
    How week 3 is reviewed
    • Items created before a server restart are still returned after it
    • All SQL queries use placeholders instead of string concatenation
    • ?search= returns only matching items and ?page=2&limit=5 returns the correct slice
    • Any unexpected error returns status 500 with JSON instead of crashing the server
    • The .db file is listed in .gitignore

    Stretch goal: Add a created_at column and support ?sort=newest and ?sort=oldest.

  4. Week 4 of 4

    User Login with JWT & API Docs

    Intermediate+2-3 hours

    Add user accounts so each person can register, log in and see only their own vault items. Finish by writing clear API documentation in your README and recording a full demo.

    What you learn

    • Hashing passwords with bcryptjs instead of storing them in plain text
    • Issuing and checking JSON Web Tokens (JWT) with jsonwebtoken
    • Protecting routes with an auth middleware
    • Keeping secrets in environment variables with a .env file

    What you submit

    • Register and login routes with hashed passwords
    • An auth middleware protecting all item routes
    • Per-user items that other users cannot read or change
    • A README with setup steps and full endpoint documentation
    How week 4 is reviewed
    • Passwords are stored only as bcrypt hashes
    • Calling an item route without a valid token returns status 401
    • User A cannot read, update or delete User B's items
    • The .env file is not committed, and a .env.example is
    • Someone else could run the project by following the README alone

    Stretch goal: Add a simple rate limit on the login route with the express-rate-limit package.

Node.js Backend internship: questions and answers

What will I build in the Node.js Backend internship?

You are assigned one of 3 projects: CloudVault: RESTful Secure API & Resource Management Hub, ChatPulse: Real-Time WebSockets Messaging & Collab Server or LinkShort: URL Shortener API. Each is a single project built up over four weekly milestones, so each week adds to the last.

What skills will I learn in the Node.js Backend internship?

The Node.js Backend internship works with Node, Express and REST APIs. Week 1: setting up a Node project with npm init and installing packages; creating an Express server and defining routes. Week 2: the four CRUD operations mapped to POST, GET, PUT/PATCH and DELETE; reading JSON request bodies with express.json(). Week 3: storing data in a SQLite database with basic SQL (CREATE, INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE); using parameterised queries to avoid SQL injection. Week 4: hashing passwords with bcryptjs instead of storing them in plain text; issuing and checking JSON Web Tokens (JWT) with jsonwebtoken.

Do I need experience to apply for the Node.js Backend internship?

You need the basics of Node, Express and REST APIs, not prior internship experience. Week 1 starts at beginner level, where you set up a Node.js project with Express and build your first API endpoints that return vault items (notes and links) from an in-memory array. Week 4 reaches intermediate+ level. A short screening quiz (8 questions, about 5 minutes) checks you are ready to start.

How is each Node.js Backend milestone reviewed?

Every week has a checklist, and a milestone is approved only when it meets all of it. For week 1 of CloudVault: RESTful Secure API & Resource Management Hub, that means: GET /api/items returns all sample items as JSON; GET /api/items/1 returns one item and GET /api/items/999 returns status 404 with an error message; GET /api/items?type=link returns only links; node_modules is not committed to Git; the server logs a message showing which port it is running on. Reviewers include engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn, and work that misses the bar comes back with notes.

What can I put on my resume after the Node.js Backend internship?

Each approved milestone gives you a line you can back up with a public LinkedIn post: Built my first REST API with Node.js and Express; Created routes with URL parameters, query filters and proper 404 responses; Tested API endpoints using Thunder Client; Built a full CRUD REST API with Node.js and Express; Added input validation and correct HTTP status codes for every route; Wrote custom logging middleware and organised routes with Express Router; Connected my Express API to a SQLite database so data persists across restarts; Added search and pagination using safe parameterised SQL queries; Built central error-handling middleware to keep the API stable; Added secure user registration and login with bcrypt and JWT to my Node.js API; Protected routes with auth middleware so each user only sees their own data; Documented every endpoint with example requests in a clear README.

What are the other projects in the Node.js Backend internship?

ChatPulse: Real-Time WebSockets Messaging & Collab Server: Build a real-time chat app with Node.js, Express and Socket.IO, with chat rooms, saved history and a simple web page to chat from. LinkShort: URL Shortener API: Build your own link shortener with Node.js and Express that turns long URLs into short codes and counts every click. Every project follows the same four-week shape, with one reviewed milestone a week.

Is the Node.js Backend internship paid? Is there a stipend?

Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month. It is performance-based and goes to the interns whose reviewed Node.js Backend work stands out in their cohort, not to every intern.

How much time does it take?

4 weeks, one milestone a week, each planned for about 2-3 hours. It is fully remote and open worldwide, so you work around college or a job.
